subsystems.label: Native mobile
subsystems.source_assessment: Current main includes the partial #1188 hosted conversation retry slice and #1196 mobile bootstrap/context isolation. The new mobile bootstrap reads a bearer from platform secure storage, requires build-time company/actor/device/surface and endpoint configuration in release, and has a retryable generic startup failure. Its own source says runtime identity/endpoints are build configuration, not authority. TitanSession still carries company/actor/device/surface but no session_revision. MobileSessionContext models server revalidation gates and MobileContextScope partitions by company, actor, device, surface and context_revision; neither is wired into the production screen/gateway or session-change lifecycle. SplashScreen loads config and constructs SurfaceSdkTitanGateway with HttpTitanSurfaceTransport only; although conversationEndpoint exists in config, HostedConversationTransport is not injected. The local ScopedOfflineCommandQueue now partitions and quarantines command intents by scope and has a restore-after-revalidation API, but it persists JSON in SharedPreferences, is not connected to a server revalidation call, does not include session_revision in MobileScopeKey, and is not a conversation/event replay queue. HostedConversationTransport carries session_id/context_revision and stable conversation, interaction, message, request, operation, correlation, trace and idempotency identities; it compares exact company/actor/device/surface/conversation/context_revision on completed responses and exposes start/continue/resume/cancel. It still sends Accept: application/json and joins the full response body before jsonDecode. Although the host response carries session_id, the client response check does not compare that field; TitanSession has no session_revision. It updates Last-Event-ID only after a completed response; reconnect() is a no-op. The host offers text/event-stream only when requested, but writes it only after dispatch returns; the mobile client currently requests JSON and neither parses live SSE nor gets durable event-log replay. Resume/cancel need a continuation token from a completed response; cancel is a follow-up request and does not abort the active request. No runtime logout, company-switch or revision-rotation hook clears in-flight request IDs, continuation/event IDs, projections or private queues. The later main commit #1199 adds inline unavailable messages for selected evidence/schedule/map/customer/commercial actions and notification/profile/attachment/voice controls until hosted scope/capabilities exist. These are client string/label heuristics, not server projection or capability authorization; generic conversation exceptions still collapse to one retry message, and startup remains generic rather than distinguishing auth, stale, unavailable and canceled outcomes. GitHub CI for #1199 passed the focused transport/context/audience step that includes the shell tests. Its tolerated legacy full-mobile diagnostic still exits nonzero: flutter analyze exit 1 and flutter test exit 1 (32 passed, 28 failed; unresolved package/import/test-source failures). Issue #1170 remains open after partial #1199; issue #1182 remains open after partial #1188; #302 and #1049 remain open after their merged partial identity/SDK slices. One native app and the distinct PWA each retain Zero/Go/Hub modes; mode names do not confer host authorization. The new #1158 mobile completion matrix is explicitly non-closing; its hosted conversation row still lists endpoint, reconnect/resume and deployed evidence as outstanding, so it does not change this source finding. No physical-device or live-host result is present.

Use server-resolved company_id/actor/device/session identity; include and compare exact session_revision and context_revision after defining safe numeric revision serialization with #302. Do not change #302 identity implementation, #1049 SDK/Server Node consumers or #811 host authority in this client lane.

Add true incremental SSE/chunk parsing and maintain the last parsed event ID during response consumption. Resume against a durable #811 server event log using the same conversation/message identity and exact still-current session/context revision. Verify interrupted stream recovery has ordered events and no duplicate consequential actions; the existing retry test proves stable identity across a transient completed-request failure only.

Bind cancel to the live HTTP request and server cancellation path; clear conversation, continuation, event IDs, projections and queued private work on logout, company switch, actor/device change or revision rotation. Connect MobileSessionContext/scope freeze and command quarantine to actual lifecycle events; keep queued command replay separate from conversation replay and use encrypted private persistence where the canonical store permits it.

Build on the #1199 subset of inline unavailable messages with typed states for unconfigured, authentication-required/revoked, stale revision, unavailable/timeout, offline, canceled and recoverable outcomes; do not treat string/label guards as server authorization. Add Flutter cases for active cancel, chunked stream/disconnect/resume, revision rotation, logout/company isolation, deduplication and unavailable host; run analyzer and the complete mobile suite, then hosted integration with correlated IDs and signed physical iOS/Android Zero/Go/Hub verification. No mock transport or successful completed-event serialization substitutes for these results.
